transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-01-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM), Mark Rodriguez (Aurelius - Procurement), Lina Park (Aurelius - Legal), Samir Patel (Aurelius - Cloud), Hannah Cole (Aurelius - Finance)
Links shared: https://redwood.example/decks/enterprise-onboarding-v3.pdf, https://redwood.example/security/dpa-sla-matrix.xlsx

Summary (auto): Quick legal triage to confirm which DPA exceptions Aurelius can accept, discussion of SLA tiers and billing entitlements, request for sandbox with KMS toggle to validate private key flow and billing samples. Next steps agreed to send redlines, provide sandbox, and reconvene with final proposed language.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate the time. we wanted to keep this tight, legal and procurement, quick alignment on the DPA exceptions you mentioned in the intake.
[00:12] Mark: Yeah thanks Jordan, um quick note, we only have 30-45 minutes on our side so if we need a deeper legal dive we'll book a follow-up. main ask from procurement: we need clarity on billing entitlements when we exceed committed volumes and how the SLA credits kick in.
[00:28] Priya: Cool, priya here. I can walk through how billing ramps, and the sandbox can show a sample invoice. quick callout: Redwood's hosted API and dedicated reservations behave slightly differently from a billing perspective re: burst capacity.
[00:43] Lina: From legal i just want to highlight the DPA exception list we sent last week. two big ones: data residency carve-outs for audit logs, and key management exception where they want either customer-managed KMS or a contractual clause that we can mandate HSM controls.
[00:59] Samir: And to add, our infra team needs guarantees on egress cost predictability — we run forecasts tightly. also, we want to avoid cross-region fallbacks unless explicitly opt-in.
[01:13] Jordan: Totally. To be explicit: we can offer a private deployment variant (we call Redwood Private) where KMS is customer-managed in the VPC; for hosted/off-the-shelf we provide KMS integrations with BYOK but there are operational caveats. i'll flag priya to show toggles.
[01:29] Priya: yeah i will demo the KMS toggle in the sandbox. note: when you flip to customer-managed keys it changes backup flow and we need an initial onboarding run with ops. it's not instant, usually a 2-3 day ops window for key sync and audit log piping.
[01:52] Mark: ok that's fine as long as we get the onboarding window and any costs spelled out. Hannah from finance is here — she wanted to confirm pricing floor for the reserved capacity and what triggers overage billing.
[02:05] Hannah: hi, thanks. specifically we need examples: if we commit to 500k tokens/day and spike to 1.2m tokens for three days, what's the billing path, and do we get pro-rata credits if response latency exceeds SLA?
[02:23] Priya: Practically, we have two levers: reserved capacity monthly commit (lower unit cost) and burst (higher unit cost). we also offer an automatic fallback policy that routes to cheaper model variants if the primary cluster is saturated. SLA credits: we have latency SLOs with a credit schedule; credits are applied when monthly latency P95 exceeds threshold. i'll attach the SLA addendum — diego will share the document.
[02:48] Diego: i'll drop the SLA addendum and price ramp sheet after the call. our price ramps typically have 3 tiers over a 90 day ramp period if you choose committed pricing.
[03:02] Lina: on DPA language — Section 5.3 we requested a carve-out for audit log residency, we cannot send audit logs to third-party regions for regulatory reasons. is that negotiable?
[03:16] Jordan: that's a fair ask. we can lock down audit log residency for the Private deployment option; for Hosted API we can offer regional retention and a contractual commitment to keep audit logs in EU/US regions as specified. one nuance: some internal monitoring events are aggregated in telemetry pipelines; we can exclude raw audit logs from that telemetry.
[03:39] Samir: when you say "exclude" does that mean those logs never leave the customer's VPC? need that clarified.
[03:44] Priya: for Private/VPC we can ensure logs remain in your VPC and we don't take custody. for hosted: logs are stored in a regional tenant and can be configured to not leave the region; but a tiny subset of anonymized metrics used for platform health could be aggregated cross-region. we'll put specific language into the DPA redline.
[04:06] [04:06] Mark: ok good. next question — indemnity caps, we've asked for a 3x revenue cap.
[04:14] Lina: right we prefer a carve-in at 3x for critical data leakage.
[04:18] Jordan: standard Redwood indemnity historically is limited to direct damages up to certain thresholds. open to discussing a commercial exception tied to committed spend. we might need procurement and legal exec sign-off for anything beyond standard.
[04:36] Hannah: budget wise we can potentially increase committed spend if pricing for Reserved capacity reflects predictable unit costs and there's a clear cap on overage exposure.
[04:46] Jordan: understood. Diego — do we have a precedent sheet for indemnity exceptions?
[04:51] Diego: yes we do, but it's usually routed via legal. i'll include past exceptions as redline examples in the doc drop.
[04:58] [05:00] Mark: on SLA credits, can you confirm whether credits are applied automatically or require a claim process? the latter adds operational overhead.
[05:07] Priya: currently credits require a claim and verification; we are piloting automated crediting on certain enterprise tiers but it's not universal. as a workaround we can include a process in the SLA addendum to streamline claims for your tier.
[05:25] Lina: also want to confirm retention windows for PII vs ephemeral tokens in logs. we need a guarantee for token-only ephemeral retention of under 30 days unless explicitly archived.
[05:36] Priya: short answer: ephemeral tokens used to produce output are retained transiently; audit logs retention is configurable. we'll map defaults and customer overrides in the DPA.
[05:46] [05:46] Jordan: quick pivot to billing entitlements. we have a few models: committed monthly, pay-as-you-go, and blended reserved with burst. in many enterprise deals we do a blended approach with a pricing floor and a capped overage.
[06:02] Hannah: can you spell out how the capped overage works? is it a hard cap or a financial protection that requires approval?
[06:08] Diego: it's financial protection where we can cap unit rates after a dollar threshold; hard technical cutoffs (i.e., forced throttle) are possible but typically undesirable. we can include a protective clause that gives you notification and an opt-in before hard throttling.
[06:25] Mark: ok we prefer notification then opt-in to throttle. fiscal risk is big for us.
[06:30] Jordan: understood. we'll propose a notification window (48 hours) + opt-in for hard throttle.
[06:36] [06:36] Lina: on DPA exceptions earlier, we've listed "no-subprocessor without prior approval" as an absolute. we understand Redwood uses cloud infra and some managed components — is complete prohibition realistic?
[06:47] Priya: realistically, we do use cloud providers as subprocessors. we can provide a list of subprocessors and agree to a notification period for any additions; we also have SOC 2 and ISO attestations to back the controls. a permanent absolute ban is uncommon and would require private/on-prem deployment.
[07:07] Samir: ok that's consistent with what we expected. next, we need to make sure that data egress costs are predictable: your pricing sheet should show worst-case egress exposure for cross-region fallbacks.
[07:18] Jordan: we'll include an appendix that outlines egress exposure scenarios. priya will include sample invoices from the sandbox run.
[07:26] [07:26] Mark: one more procurement-points list: 1) final DPA language, 2) SLA addendum with credit schedule, 3) pricing ramp and overage caps, 4) sandbox run with KMS BYOK demo, 5) operational onboarding timeline. can we get those by next week?
[07:42] Diego: yes, we'll aim to send that packet by 2027-01-29.
[07:48] Lina: on the DPA redline: we may send alternate language for Sections 7 and 11 (data export and audit) because of regulatory nuance in EMEA.
[07:57] Priya: understood. Priya again — small note: when you run the sandbox with BYOK you may see different tokenization rates due to telemetry; we'll annotate expected variance.
[08:09] Hannah: about billing: if we move to Reserved capacity, do you require prepay or can it be monthly invoiced with net30?
[08:16] Jordan: standard is net30 invoice monthly for enterprise; prepay is optional if you want discounted comps. we'll include both options on the price sheet.
[08:26] [08:26] Mark: switching to security review — we want to confirm SOC2 scope and whether there's an option for a customer-specific pen test.
[08:36] Diego: SOC2 Type II is available; we can provide the report under NDA. for customer-specific pen test we allow a coordinated test with our security team and a narrow scoping window. we do require a blackout window for high-impact tests.
[08:51] Lina: please note we may want to schedule a targeted pen test against the Private deployment if we go that route.
[08:57] Priya: noted.
[09:02] [09:02] Samir: regarding network-level controls, we need to confirm whether egress filtering and dedicated IPs are available in dedicated reserved pools.
[09:11] Priya: dedicated pools can side-car into your VPC with static egress IP options; we'll document those constraints.
[09:18] Mark: great. are there any competitors who do this differently that we should be aware of? we looked at a few other vendors — how does Redwood differentiate on this exact use-case?
[09:29] Jordan: quick comparison: some vendors push customers to self-host entirely; Redwood tries to offer a spectrum — hosted with strong regional controls, dedicated with reserved pools for performance and billing predictability, and private for full control. our edge is the routing/fallback policies + cost-aware controls.
[09:46] [09:46] Lina: one last DPA nit — we asked for a two year data retention limit for non-PII telemetry and a 30 day limit for PII tokens unless explicitly archived.
[09:58] Priya: we can map that, with the caveat that certain logs required for forensic/incident response may be retained longer but under stricter access controls.
[10:10] Jordan: ok i want to summarize the outcomes and next steps so nothing is lost.
[10:14] Jordan: 1) Redwood to send redlined DPA highlighting exceptions and proposed language (Jordan) by 2027-01-29. 2) Redwood to provision limited sandbox with BYOK/KMS toggle and sample invoice (Priya) by 2027-02-02. 3) Redwood to share SLA addendum, price ramp sheet and indemnity precedent examples (Diego) by 2027-01-29. 4) Aurelius to confirm internal commit levels and note mandatory DPA clauses (Hannah/Lina) by 2027-02-04.
[10:36] Mark: sounds good. any blockers?
[10:39] Lina: only timing on legal review. if we get the packet next week we can react quickly.
[10:44] Jordan: perfect. we'll aim to get the packet in your inbox friday. thanks everyone.
[10:50] [10:50] Closing notes: casual cross-talk about holiday schedules, Diego mentions internal playbook link, Priya drops a note about sandbox credentials will be ephemeral.
